name: SPE1 Case 1 three-dimensional black-oil benchmark
physics_regime: Finite-deformation solid-reference four-phase mixture benchmark with one deformable solid matrix phase and water, oil, and gas fluid phases, converted explicitly to SI units from SPE1 Case 1.

manuscript_basis.role: Water, stock-tank oil, and stock-tank gas component storage through B_w, B_o, B_g, and R_s.
assumptions_added: The official PVTW, PVDG, and PVTO tables define the benchmark fluid closure.
SPE1 Case 1 specifies DRSDT=0, so dissolved gas remains at its initialized R_s while injected gas accumulates as free gas.

manuscript_basis.role: Retain the Bedford--Drumheller transfer potential tau and chemical-potential representation while specializing the storage and phase-equilibrium data to SPE1 black oil.
assumptions_added: The thermodynamic reference gauge is stated explicitly and cannot be inferred from PVT tables alone.

The equilibrium phase-appearance limit must be recovered from equality of the gas-component potentials; any finite nonequilibrium transfer resistance is an untuned model extension and receives a separate sensitivity study.

manuscript_basis.role: Phase Darcy flux with tabulated relative permeability, pressure-dependent viscosity, heterogeneous layer permeability, and gravity.
Water and gas pressure reconstruction from oil pressure; the SPE1 tables set both capillary curves to zero.
Finite-deformation solid and fluid component storage, solid-reference fluxes, deformable-skeleton momentum, and pressure-stress coupling.
assumptions_added: The phase registry contains matrix, water, oil, and gas.
Solid displacement and the solid-reference Jacobian are solved rather than prescribed as J=1.

variables.name: ux uy uz
variables.meaning: Q2 continuous-Galerkin displacement of the deformable solid skeleton.

variables.name: oil_pressure
variables.meaning: P1 continuous backbone of the enriched-Galerkin oil reference pressure.

variables.name: oil_pressure_enrichment
variables.meaning: P0 enrichment of the oil reference pressure; the constitutive and flux operators consume the reconstructed total pressure.

variables.name: tau
variables.meaning: P1 continuous backbone of the Bedford--Drumheller transfer potential evolved by the manuscript transfer-work equation.

variables.name: tau_enrichment
variables.meaning: P0 enrichment of tau; all transfer-work and conversion objects consume the reconstructed P1+P0 field.

variables.name: water_saturation
variables.meaning: Continuous-Galerkin water saturation used by the parent black-oil CG/EG architecture.

variables.name: gas_saturation
variables.meaning: Continuous-Galerkin gas saturation used by the parent black-oil CG/EG architecture.

variables.name: solution_gas_oil_ratio
variables.meaning: Continuous-Galerkin dissolved solution gas-oil ratio retained at its initialized value by the DRSDT=0 history equation.

mesh.description: Three-dimensional Q2/EG finite-element representation of the official SPE1 10 x 10 x 3 Cartesian geometry converted to SI. The compatible element policy and mapping of layers, completions, and report blocks must be documented and mesh-converged; it must not be described as the official 300-cell discretization unless it is exactly that discretization.

boundary_conditions: No-flow component flux on every external reservoir boundary.
Internal INJ completion at (1,1,1) with gas-rate control and 9014 psia maximum BHP.
Internal PROD completion at (10,10,3) with 20000 STB/day maximum oil rate and 1000 psia minimum BHP.

Mechanically admissible external data and minimal rigid-body constraints for the deformable skeleton, traced to the finite-deformation momentum weak form and documented as a benchmark modeling choice.
initial_conditions: EQUIL datum pressure is 4800 psia at 8400 ft.
Water-oil contact is 8450 ft and gas-oil contact is 8300 ft with zero tabulated capillary pressure.
Initial dissolved gas-oil ratio is 1.270 Mscf/STB throughout 8300-8450 ft.
The initial solid displacement is zero; subsequent solid deformation and J are solved from the coupled mixture equations.

execution.type: Fully coupled transient finite-deformation solid-reference Newton solve with adaptive step cuts at well-control and phase-appearance events.
execution.solver_notes: Use Q2 continuous-Galerkin displacement, P1+P0 enriched-Galerkin reconstructed pressure with its required facet and weak boundary terms, the parent continuous black-oil state fields, field scaling, a coupled block preconditioner, and the official monthly TSTEP sequence. Cell-centered finite volume and imposed J=1 are diagnostic reductions only and cannot satisfy this specification.

outputs: Field oil production rate and gas-oil ratio.
Injector and producer block pressures and well BHP.
Gas saturation at the nine official report blocks.
Injector/producer oil, water, and gas rates and cumulative volumes.
Per-step water, oil, and gas component global-balance defects.
Tau backbone, enrichment, reconstructed field, and evolution residual.
Phase/component chemical potentials, gas-transfer affinity, and phase-equilibrium residual.
Onsager or phase-transfer dissipation and conversion-insertion momentum contribution.
Pressure and saturation restart snapshots.

observables: BGSAT at the nine official blocks
WBHP and phase rates for INJ and PROD
validation.pass_fail: Acceptance requires the coupled finite-deformation CG/EG implementation with active reconstructed tau, chemical-potential and transfer-affinity closures, thermodynamic identities, nonnegative mechanismwise dissipation, conversion-insertion momentum accounting, AD/PETSc Jacobian, solid and fluid component balances, phase-volume closure, momentum balance, and mesh/time-step convergence gates to pass with zero required skips. OPM rate, pressure, saturation, and cumulative differences are reported as comparison metrics without post-hoc tuning; an FV, imposed-J, or phase-transforming black-oil-only algebraic reduction cannot satisfy acceptance.

open_questions: Construct and document a thermodynamic extension of the SPE1 PVT tables that supplies chemical-potential differences and their derivatives while reproducing the tabulated formation-volume factors and saturated Rs curve; SPE1 does not provide absolute chemical-potential reference data.
Treat finite phase-transfer/Onsager resistance as an explicitly declared nonequilibrium extension with sensitivity analysis because SPE1 supplies no kinetic coefficient; do not tune it to OPM output.
Replace the fixed-skeleton/FV benchmark path with a genuine coupled four-phase finite-deformation Q2/EG solve and quantify its comparison to the pinned OPM reference.
Resolve and document the mechanically admissible SPE1 skeleton boundary conditions and constitutive data without tuning to OPM outputs.
Resolve a verified Q2/EG mesh policy that preserves the official layer, completion, and report-block mapping and perform spatial convergence.
Extend the verified one-cell FV well controller to aggregate pressure and rate over multiple completion cells.
Generate a pinned OPM reference summary for the exact manifest commit.
